name: Bucket Bronco
beta: Ease up simple rock to a ledge on the left, then follow the brown plated section, clipping two bolts; one more bolt sits on the final headwall.
overview: Easy rock leads up and left to a ledge, then brown plates on the face carry past two bolts. One more bolt sits on the final headwall.

current.area_walk_in: The way in passes through a notch in the rock before reaching the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 25 ft left of the notch the approach passes through

name: Buckwheat's Bender
beta: Before reaching the high first bolt, you may be able to sling knobs and slot small cams.
overview: Three-bolt line on the spire's southern shoulder, beginning at the spire base on its low southern end.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Low on the southern toe, the first rock you meet

name: Buffalo Soldier
beta: Follow the series of cracks that slant rightward, clipping four bolts.
overview: Four bolts protect a string of rightward-slanting cracks, starting about 15 ft to the right of Apartheid and Dial Africa.

current.area_walk_in: Two ways in. Starting at the rear loop of Hidden Valley Campground, head roughly north in the direction of Echo Cove; the formation sits about halfway along. Or leave the car at Echo Cove, follow the old road southwest, then take the climber trail that branches right to the rock.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 15 ft right of where Baby Apes and its neighbour begin

name: Bulkhead Arete
beta: Begin to the right of the neighboring route, angling rightward to reach the northwest arete, which leads to a bolt; higher, traverse rightward over the west face to finish.
overview: Angle up and right onto the northwest arete, stay on it as far as a bolt, then continue up and rightward across the west face.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: just right of the previous route

name: Bummer
beta: Gear needed runs to about two inches, with tiny pieces up to an inch especially useful. A single frustrating step reaches a tiny crystalline hole.
overview: A baffling move reaches a small crystalline pocket. The bolt up high on pitch two feels a touch spooky to clip, and the route carries some vegetation.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the Lower Yosemite Fall trail to the bridge, cross it, and continue a short way east. A climbers' path leaves the trail and a brief scramble gets you to the foot of the cliff.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Vin Ordinaire
beta: Ascend the scoop with minimal protection until a fixed piton on the right, then continue leftward and upward toward a bolt. One medium tricam can be placed between the two initial fixed points. Climb the chute directly as it gets steeper; mid-size Friends and tricams fit pockets on the unprotected stretch to the last bolt, and the belay is atop the Rappel Route.
overview: Climbs a narrow gully on the dome's north side, round the corner from the Rappel Route. A bold scoop leads to a Lost Arrow already in place, then the line moves leftward to a bolt and goes directly up the increasingly steep gully, with a sizable gap to the last bolt. The bolts may be suspect.

current.area_walk_in: Look to the left roughly fifty feet short of where the High Peaks path meets the Tunnel path; the pinnacle there is marked by a concave scoop.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: belay is shared with the Rappel Route's top
current.location: narrow gully on the north side, round the corner from the Rappel Route

name: Burtons Below
beta: Ascend the water-carved chute beside Lost Fortune on four bolts, carry on over the gentle face clipping two more, and a final bolt guards the overhanging step onto the summit.
overview: Follows a water chute, crosses an easy face, and ends with a pleasant, exposed overhang finish at the summit.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Lost Fortune's neighbour on the left, in the water-carved gully

name: Bury Me With My Boots On
beta: Begin as the preceding route does, then work rightward to a bolted ledge. The next pitch, over 165 feet long, goes by six bolts up to a second belay station with bolts; to leave, traverse directly right.
overview: From the bolted ledge, one very long pitch passes six bolts to a second bolted belay. Escape is by traversing straight right, though a direct finish looks plausible.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: begins with the same moves as Cactus Pete's, then moves out right to a bolted ledge

name: Bush Blows Chips
beta: Begin with a crack then clip four bolts above it, finishing at a bolt anchor.

current.area_walk_in: The Tiger Rocks are paler boulders and crags uphill and left of the brown boulders.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: tallest wall of the cluster, nearly above another route and uphill-left of the large rock

name: Bye Gully
beta: Easy third-class scrambling except a roughly 10-foot flared chimney partway up, the only fifth-class section, which is much easier to downclimb than to climb.
overview: A mostly third-class gully along the left edge of the Weeping Wall with one short flaring chimney; mainly used as the way down.

current.descent: used as a descent route; rope down into it from the wall
current.location: The gully at the far left edge of the Weeping Wall

name: Cake Walk
beta: Follow the dike on the adjacent rock behind, using its lone bolt, up to a bolted anchor for rappelling.
overview: Runs up a dike on the second formation, finishing at a belay that doubles as a rappel point. It extends the dike seen lower down, which also forms the Rock 1 descent and the neighbouring Short Cake.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: belay on bolts and rap point
current.location: Rock 2, one step behind the first formation

name: Carousel
beta: The southern top of the rock carries four bolts that serve as the toprope anchor.
overview: A top-rope zone on the biggest rock in the cluster, offering lines ranging upward from low fifth class to a stiff 5.10 around its 18-foot mass.

current.area_walk_in: Take the faint path leaving the High Peaks route ahead of the Anvil and climb to the biggest rock of the cluster.

name: Castles Burning

overview: A brown face with five bolts and a few bulges; rope drag needs managing.

name: Casual Affair
beta: Step off a boulder to begin, and follow the edge up; a bolt appears about 20 feet up.

name: Catchy
beta: The crux is a hard, clumsy step to surmount a big bulge; this is the tallest line on the formation, with eight bolts to the anchor.
overview: The tallest climb of the Bubble, hardest where a bulge must be surmounted.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Aretile Dysfunction
beta: Stay along the arete's left side; past the third bolt, move rightward over the arete onto the slabbier rock.
overview: Hugs the leftmost side of the arete; once the last bolt is clipped, the line slips across the arete onto the slabbier rock higher up.

current.area_walk_in: The walk-in to these formations is a long one, roughly 1.4 miles.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: on the arete, along its leftmost side

name: Central Pillar of Frenzy
beta: Most parties stop after the fifth pitch and rappel, or add an extra pair of pitches and traverse to a neighboring route to rappel, or carry on to the upper ledges. Thin protection is needed on the upper section.
overview: Parties usually bail after the fifth pitch by rapping, or go two pitches higher and cross over to another line to descend, or press on to the big ledge system and leave through the bowl. The upper part demands extra-thin gear.

current.area_walk_in: Climbers' trails leave the south-side road; the East Buttress base is roughly 20 minutes up the trail. Other routes, such as those starting from the Gunsight notch, take longer and involve scrambling.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Cream of Weak
beta: Angle up and rightward by two bolts, then step right into cracks of easier difficulty.
overview: Two bolts guard the start, after which the route eases into simpler cracks.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Six ft along the wall from Quaking Oats, rightward

name: Chancroid
beta: The hard moves are right at the start, as far as the third bolt; above that the climbing relaxes into easy ground to the anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Charles Who?
beta: Follow the flake as it bends up toward the right, then continue by three bolts.

name: Chicago Nipple Slump
beta: Set a toprope on the rust-hued arete beside the previous route, on its right; it merges with that route at the final bolt.
overview: Top-rope up a rust-coloured arete, merging with its neighbour at that route's last bolt.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Chouinard-Herbert
beta: Protection is mostly nuts. The start and finish are inelegant, while the middle part of the route is enjoyable and exposed.
overview: The start and finish are rather inelegant, while the heart of the route is airy and rewarding.

current.area_walk_in: Climb the trail for about a mile to the stream flowing off the rock east side, then follow the streambed a few hundred feet and cross to the obvious ramp that starts a long third-class scramble up and right to the foot of the Flying Buttress pillar. West-face routes lie round the corner from there; north-face routes need more ledge scrambling up and left.
current.descent: Head south from the summit to the notch, then go down a class 2 chute (loose in places) eastward to a stream, and keep dropping to reach the trail.

name: Chouinard's Crack
beta: Gear needed up to about four inches. The crack is deceptive; the hardest moves are in the first twenty feet.
overview: A traditional crack line. The hard part: less than 20 ft off the ground.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Citizen Fish
beta: Start with face moves past a bolt before reaching the crack.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the nature trail to the arch, then go straight on along a well-trodden track that dips, crosses a dry wash and climbs a hill. Turn right at the top and continue a short way to the brown slab.

name: Claim Jumper
beta: Begin behind a tree, to the right side of B-Movie, in a crack that fades, then continue on the face by three bolts up to the summit.
overview: The crack fades out, and face climbing past three bolts finishes the route.

current.location: Begins in the next crack over, immediately beside B-Movie, before it fades onto the face

overview: Bolted line that begins from a ten-foot boulder, crosses grey flakes, then finishes with face moves on the way up to the summit.

current.area_walk_in: From the gravel lot by Echo Rock, follow the trail past the south end of Echo Rock and cross open desert toward the southwest face of Little Hunk. The trail fades near the end; just before the wall, bear right and scramble through brush and boulders to the base.

overview: A full-length pitch featuring thrilling moves en route to the summit of Tiburcio’s X.
